newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in featureless trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. October consumer price index and retail sales and weekly jobless claims data, dealers said on Thursday.
The consumer price index for October is forecast to be unchanged from September's increase of 0.3 percent.
October retail sales is expected to show a gain of 0.3 percent against September's 0.7 percent increase.
Weekly jobless claims is expected to rise to 334,000 from 331,000 in the previous week.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on lack of fresh factors. Some players are waiting for possible direction from tonight's release of the CPI, retail sales and weekly jobless claims figures," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact here as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday, weekend and week-fixed were unchanged from Wedneday's common 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8, six-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 and nine-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
